title: GPU Fleet & Infra Playbook: Capacity, Cloud Accounts, IaC Modules, CI/CD and Runbooks
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference engineering standards and operational procedures for GPU fleet capacity planning, cloud accounts and networking, Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD build pipelines, and the primary infra runbooks used by oncall and capacity teams. The goal is to provide a single, actionable source of truth for day-2 operations, onboarding new infra engineers, and performing safe changes to GPU provisioning and infrastructure modules.

Scope:
- Applies to all hosted, dedicated, and private deployment infrastructure managed by eng-infra that uses the centralized GPU fleet and shared cloud accounts.
- Covers: capacity forecasting, allocation policy, VPC/subnet/account design, IaC module standards (Terraform/Terragrunt), CI/CD pipeline patterns, and production runbooks for common operational tasks.

Who should use this document:
- Infra engineers, SREs, platform engineers, and oncall rotation members.
- Owners of Dedicated customer clusters, Private deployment packaging, and Autoscaling policies.

High-level architecture (summary):
- GPU Fleet: virtual pools of GPU nodes (k8s nodepools / managed instance groups) organized by capability class (A100-80GB, A100-40GB, H100, L4) and tenancy (shared-hosted, reserved-dedicated, private).
- Control plane: internal orchestration service (fleet-manager) that maps inference requests to pools using routing policies.
- Provisioning: Terraform modules + Terragrunt wrappers create cloud accounts, VPCs, subnets, IAM roles, and GPU instance groups. CI/CD pipelines validate and apply IaC changes to staging before production.

Responsibilities and owners:
- Fleet Capacity: eng-infra/capacity-team (owner: Marcus Ng) - responsible for forecasting, quota requests, and capacity increases.
- Cloud Accounts & Networking: eng-infra/cloud-platform (owner: Lena Thompson) - account provisioning, VPC design, peering and transit.
- IaC Modules: infra-iac (owner: Aisha Patel) - maintain terraform modules, module registry, and upgrade cadence.
- CI/CD & Build: eng-infra/ci (owner: Diego Martinez) - pipelines, testing gates, and release automation.
- Oncall & Runbooks: eng-sre oncall rotation - first responders for incidents affecting capacity or provisioning.

Capacity planning and KPIs:
- Target utilization bands per pool: 60-80% (steady state).
- Scale buffer: maintain at least 20% headroom to meet P95 burst demand for hosted API tier.
- SLOs: median pod startup time < 60s for warm pools; cold start P95 < 300s for new instance provisioning; quota fulfillment lead time for reserved Dedicated requests < 5 business days.
- Metrics to track: available_gpus, allocated_gpus, pending_provisioning, avg_pod_startup_ms, failed_allocations_count.
- Reporting cadence: weekly capacity digest, monthly forecast with 12-week runway.

Allocation policy and tagging:
- Tagging is mandatory on all resources: team, owner, environment, cost_center, project, compliance_scope. Example tags: team:eng-infra, owner:eng-infra/capacity, environment:prod.
- Naming convention: {env}-{region}-{service}-{resource-type}-{short-id} (e.g., prod-us-west1-gpufleet-nodepool-a100-01).
- Priority queueing: dedicated > private > hosted API > low-priority internal jobs. Preemption rules are enforced by K8s node taints and scheduler tiers.

Cloud accounts & networking patterns:
- Per-environment accounts: prod, staging, dev; with additional customer-dedicated accounts for Hosted-Dedicated mode when isolation is required.
- VPC design: single VPC per account, segmented by subnet (mgmt, control-plane, inference, logging). Subnet sizing: reserve /20 for inference subnets per region for initial capacity.
- Cross-account access: AWS Resource Access Manager or IAM Cross-account roles; GCP uses Shared VPCs with Host Projects for central networking.
- Egress controls: NAT gateways in dedicated subnets; egress filtering via proxy for Private deployments.

Terraform / IaC modules (standards and examples):
- Module rules:
  1) Modules must be versioned in the registry and include CHANGELOG.md and upgrade notes.
  2) No hardcoded account IDs in modules; inputs must be parametric.
  3) Modules should expose tag map, name prefix, and optional lifecycle controls (create_before_destroy where safe).
- Common module inventory (registry names):
  - redwood_vpc (owner: cloud-platform, versions: 1.3.0+)
  - redwood_subnet (owner: cloud-platform)
  - redwood_iam_roles (owner: infra-iac)
  - redwood_gpu_nodepool (owner: infra-iac)
  - redwood_k8s_addons (owner: infra-platform)

Example terraform snippet (nodepool):
module "gpu_nodepool" {
  source = "registry.internal.redwood/redwood_gpu_nodepool"
  version = "~> 2.1.0"

  name_prefix = "prod-us-west1-gpufleet"
  machine_type = "n1-standard-32"
  accelerator_type = "A100-80GB"
  accelerator_count = 4
  min_size = 2
  max_size = 200
  tags = local.default_tags
}

Module lifecycle and upgrades:
- Major versions require a written upgrade plan, upgrade playbook entry, and at least one canary account run.
- Deprecation policy: 90 days notice for minor versions, 180 days for major versions, with automated CI warnings on PRs that use deprecated module versions.

CI/CD and pipeline patterns:
- Pipeline stages for IaC: lint -> unit tests (terratest) -> plan (in ephemeral workspace) -> integration apply to staging -> smoke tests -> manual approval -> apply to production.
- Branch rules: all changes to infra modules require PRs and 2+ reviewers including module owner; destructive changes must include runbook updates and scheduled maintenance window.
- Pipeline guardrails: plan files stored and validated; auto-rollback on failed post-apply smoke tests; approvals required for any plan that changes resources in prod account.
- Secrets: KMS/HSM-backed secrets via vault; no plaintext secrets in CI logs.

Build artifacts and registries:
- Module registry: internal Terraform registry (artifacts signed and versioned).
- Container images: built in CI via kaniko/buildkit, signed, and stored in internal registry with immutable tags.

Runbooks and operational procedures (main playbooks):
1) Increase GPU Capacity (planned request)
   - Trigger: capacity forecast shows <12 weeks runway or weekly available_gpus < (expected_peak * 1.2).
   - Steps:
     1. Open capacity request ticket in Jira (template: Capacity Request). Include projected usage, customer owners, region, instance type, and justification.
     2. Run cost estimate and expected lead times with cloud vendor quoting.
     3. Prepare terraform changes in a dedicated branch: increase max_size and desired_count; run plan in staging account.
     4. Schedule maintenance window if nodepool resizing could affect latency (notify SRE and product owners).
     5. Apply change to prod after approval; monitor available_gpus and pod startup metrics.
     6. Post-change: update capacity dashboard and close Jira.

2) Emergency Scale-Up (hotfix for surge)
   - Trigger: sudden spike causes pending_provisioning > 5% and degraded tail latency.
   - Steps:
     1. Pager triggers oncall; oncall evaluates metrics and current quotas.
     2. If quota exhausted, exec the quota escalation playbook: contact cloud-account-owner and submit emergency quota request with priority.
     3. If quotas available, perform a controlled manual scale: increase nodepool desired_count by 20% and set max_size accordingly.
     4. Monitor health and revert or further increase as needed.

3) Deprovisioning Nodepool
   - Trigger: nodepool or instance family is end-of-life, or cost optimization requirement.
   - Steps:
     1. Create migration plan for workloads (cordon and drain nodes, migrate PVCs).
     2. Run compatibility tests on replacement node types.
     3. Update terraform to remove nodepool and apply in staging, then prod after smoke tests.

Monitoring, alerts and dashboards:
- Core dashboards: GPU Capacity Overview, Nodepool Health, Pod Start Times, Allocation Failures, Cost Per Token estimator.
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - CRIT: allocated_gpus / available_gpus > 0.98 for > 10 minutes.
  - HIGH: pod_startup_p95 > 300s.
  - MED: pending_provisioning > 5% for 30m.
- Runbooks must be referenced in alert descriptions with direct links to the Jira playbook and pager duty escalation.

Change management and release windows:
- Non-destructive infra changes may be scheduled 24x7; any change affecting production nodepools or network topology requires a 48-hour notice and a scheduled window (default maintenance hours: Tue/Wed 02:00-06:00 UTC).
- Emergency changes must be documented after the fact in the change log and reviewed by the change advisory board (weekly).

Oncall and escalation:
- Primary oncall: eng-sre first responder. Escalation: eng-infra capacity -> cloud-platform -> product owner for customer-impacting events.
- Pager duty run: P0 incidents page to include runbook link, list of impacted services, and communication templates for status page and customer updates.

Operational runbook appendix (quick commands and checks):
- Check available GPUs (Grafana/Prometheus query): sum(gpu_available) by region
- Check pending allocations: sum(gpu_pending) by queue
- Quick scale (k8s): kubectl scale nodepool/gpupool --replicas=<n> --context=prod-cluster
- Terraform plan and apply (recommended): make -C infra/modules/gpu_nodepool plan TARGET_ACCOUNT=prod && make -C infra/modules/gpu_nodepool apply TARGET_ACCOUNT=prod

Postmortem and retrospectives:
- Any P1/P0 incident triggered by capacity or provisioning must have a postmortem published within 72 hours. Postmortem owners: oncall primary + capacity lead. Runbook updates must be added as an action item.

Appendix: sample PR checklist for IaC changes:
- Include CHANGELOG entry for module version bump.
- Attach plan output and show diff for resources in prod.
- Confirm no hardcoded credentials.
- Add or update runbook if behavior or recovery steps change.
- 2 reviewers including module owner; at least one SRE reviewer for production-impacting changes.

References and related pages:
- Infra IaC modules: /confluence/eng-infra/terraform-and-iac/infra-iac-modules-ci-cd-guidelines-2026.json
- GPU capacity runbook: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026.json

Document maintenance:
- Owners must review this playbook quarterly and after any major fleet change.
- For proposed edits: submit a PR to the confluence content git repo with rationale and cross-links to module PRs.
